t:
Match the column I, II and III and choose the correct combination from the options given below
[[img:ca59f388d1c7]]
s: Actinomorphic flowers show radial symmetry and can be divided into equal halves by any radial plane, as in chilli (a-2-R). Zygomorphic flowers show bilateral symmetry, divisible in only one plane, as in Gulmohar (b-1-P). Asymmetric flowers are irregular, not divisible by any plane, as in Canna (c-3-Q). This combination is option B.

t: Consider the following statements:
s: Statement D is correct: in monocot seeds such as maize, the plumule is enclosed in a sheath called the coleoptile and the radicle in a sheath called the coleorhiza. These protective sheaths cover the shoot and root tips during germination. The keyed answer identifies this as the correct description of the monocot embryo.
o: When ovules are borne on central axis and septa are absent, as in Dianthus and Primrose the placentation is free central
In some seeds such as castor the endosperm formed as a result of double fertilization , is a food storing tissue.

t:
Which of the following statements is / are true :
a) Pneumatophores help to get oxygen for respiration.
b) In some plants such as Australian acacia the leaves are small and short lived
c) The leaf is attached to the stem by the leaf base and may bear two lateral small leaf like structures called leaf lets.
d) The lamina is the green expanded part of the leaf with veins and veinlets.
s: a is true: pneumatophores of mangroves like Rhizophora grow upward and help get oxygen for respiration. b is true: in Australian acacia the leaves are small and short-lived, and petioles become green phyllodes. d is true: the lamina is the green expanded part with veins and veinlets. c is false because the lateral leaf-like structures at the leaf base are stipules, not leaflets.

t:
Read the following statements :
(i) A sterile stamen is called staminode
(ii) Epipetalous stamen is found in lily and an epiphyllous stamen in brinjal
(iii) China rose possess polyadelphous stamen
(iv) Salvia and mustard possess variable length filaments in stamen
(v) Pea possess monoadelphous as well as diadelphous stamen
How many of the above statements are correct?
s: Correct: (i) a sterile stamen is a staminode, and (iv) filament length varies within the flower in Salvia and mustard. Wrong: (ii) is reversed, as epipetalous stamens occur in brinjal and epiphyllous in lily; (iii) China rose has monoadelphous stamens, polyadelphous is citrus; (v) pea is diadelphous only. So two statements are correct.

t: Which one is not related to roots in monocotyledons plants?
s: In monocots the primary root does arise from the radicle of the embryo but is short-lived, and it is replaced by many roots arising from the base of the stem, forming a fibrous root system. Hence the statement that the root never originates from the radicle is not true of monocots, while A, C and D describe them correctly.
o: The primary root is short lived
Root never originates from the radicle part of embryo
Roots originate from the base of the stem

t:
Assertion (A) : Grasses and strawberry perform vegetative propagation.
Reason (R) : Their sub-arial stems spread to new niches when older parts die and new plants are formed.
s: Grasses and strawberry have runners and stolons, slender lateral sub-aerial branches that spread over the ground. When older parts die, the rooted nodes develop into new independent plants, giving vegetative propagation and allowing spread to new niches. So both statements are true and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

t:
Match the column I and II choose the correct combination from the options given
[[img:cd834f758438]]
s: Placenta as a ridge along the ventral suture is marginal (a-4, pea). Placenta at the base of the ovary is basal (b-3, sunflower). Ovules on a central axis with no septa is free central (c-2, Dianthus). Ovules on the inner wall or periphery is parietal (d-5, mustard). Placenta axile with ovules attached is axile (e-1, China rose). Hence option B.

t: Epigynous flowers with inferior ovary are found in
s: In epigynous flowers the thalamus margin grows up and fuses with the ovary wall, so other floral parts arise above the ovary, which is inferior. Examples are guava, cucumber and the ray florets of sunflower. Mustard, China rose and brinjal are hypogynous, and plum, rose and peach are perigynous with half-inferior ovary. Hence C.
o: Guava, Cucumber, Ray florets of sun flower

t:
Which of the following statements is /are true :
i) Stem tendrils which develop from axillary buds, are slender and spirally coiled and help plants to climb.
ii) Axillary buds of stems may also get modified into woody, straight and pointed spines
iii) Leaves are the most important vegetative organs for photosynthesis
iv) Leaves of dicotyledonous plants generally possess reticulate venation; while parallel venation is the characteristic of most monocotyledons.
s:
Correct Answer: (C) i, iii & iv

Statement (i) is true as stem tendrils are slender, spirally coiled structures arising from axillary buds that aid in climbing (e.g., gourds, grapevines). 
Statement (ii) is false because axillary buds modify into woody, straight, and pointed thorns, not spines (spines are modified leaves or leaf parts as seen in cacti). 
Statements (iii) and (iv) are true since leaves are the primary vegetative organs performing photosynthesis, with dicots typically showing reticulate venation and monocots showing parallel venation.

Options (A), (B), and (D) are incorrect because they all include statement (ii), which wrongly uses the term spines instead of thorns.

t: Choose which is applicable to solanaceae
s: Flowers of Solanaceae (potato family) have a bicarpellary syncarpous gynoecium with the ovary obliquely placed, and axile placentation on a swollen placenta bearing many ovules. Tetradynamous stamens (4 long, 2 short) are characteristic of mustard (Brassicaceae), not Solanaceae. Hence both obliquely placed ovary and swollen placenta apply.

t:
Select the statements which are true :
a) Fruit formed without fertilization is called parthenocarpic fruit.
b) The fruit wall is called perisperm, may be dry or fleshy.
c) When the pericarp is thick and fleshy as in Mango, it is differentiated into an outer thin epicarp, middle fleshy mesocarp and the inner hard endocarp.
d) Due to the presence of hard and stony endocarp, drupes are called, stone fruits.
e) The edible part of Coconut is the mesocarp.
s: a is true: fruit formed without fertilisation is parthenocarpic. c is true: the fleshy pericarp of mango shows epicarp, fleshy mesocarp and hard endocarp. d is true: drupes are stone fruits due to the stony endocarp. b is false because the fruit wall is the pericarp, not perisperm; e is false since the edible part of coconut is the endosperm. Hence a, c, d.

t:
Assertion : Syngenesious condition is a type of cohesion of stamens
Reason : In this condition filaments remain free and anthers are united
s: Cohesion is the union of stamens among themselves. In the syngenesious condition, as in sunflower (Asteraceae), the anthers are fused into a tube while the filaments remain free. The reason describes exactly this arrangement, which is why syngenesy is classed as a type of cohesion of stamens. Both statements true and R explains A.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

t: Correct position of floral parts on thalamus in mustard plant is
s: Mustard has a hypogynous flower: the gynoecium occupies the highest position on the thalamus and the sepals, petals and stamens are inserted below it, so the ovary is superior. B describes epigynous flowers (guava), while C and D describe perigynous flowers (plum, rose, peach) with a half-inferior ovary. Hence A.
o: Gynoecium occupies in the highest position, while the other parts are situated below it
Margin of the thalamus grows upwards, enclosing the ovary completely and other parts arise below the ovary
Gynoecium is present in the centre and other parts cover it partially
Gynoecium is situated at the centre and other parts of the flower are located at the rim of the thalamus, at the same level

t:
Study the following statements and choose the correct option
I) Buds are present in the axil of leaflets of the compound leaf
II) Pulvinus leaf base is present in some leguminous plants
III) In Alstonia, the petioles expand, become green and synthesize food.
IV) In guava opposite phyllotaxy is observed
s: II is correct: the swollen pulvinus leaf base occurs in some leguminous plants. IV is correct: guava (and Calotropis) show opposite phyllotaxy. I is wrong because buds occur in the axil of the petiole of a compound leaf, not in the axils of leaflets. III is wrong: green expanded petioles are seen in Australian acacia; Alstonia has whorled phyllotaxy.
o: II and IV are correct but I and III are wrong
I and III are correct but II and IV are wrong
I and IV are correct but II and III are wrong
II, III and IV are correct but I is wrong

t: Identify the correct statements related to underground stem modification
s: Underground stems such as potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand and Colocasia store food and act as organs of perennation, helping the plant survive unfavourable conditions. Their buds (eyes, nodes) also give rise to new plants, so they help in vegetative propagation. Being underground and non-green, they do not carry out photosynthesis. Hence both 1 and 3.
o: They act as organs of perennation to tide over conditions unfavourable for growth

t:
Observe the following placentation and identify a plant which possess it
[[img:14284d438adb]]
s: The figure shows a multilocular ovary with septa and ovules attached to a central placental axis, which is axile placentation. It occurs in China rose, tomato and lemon. Dianthus shows free central placentation (no septa), Argemone shows parietal placentation, and sunflower shows basal placentation. Hence China rose.

t:
Which among the following features are shared by Mustard and Tomato ?
a) Bisexual flower
b) Axile placentation
c) Parietal placentation
d) Actinomorphic symmetry
e) Tap root system
s: Both mustard and tomato have bisexual (a), actinomorphic (d) flowers and dicot tap root systems (e). They differ in placentation: mustard (Brassicaceae) has parietal placentation with a false septum, while tomato (Solanaceae) has axile placentation. So b and c are not shared. Hence a, d and e only.

t:
Assertion (A) : When the stem is young or primary in nature, it is green in colour.
Reason (R) : Most of the angiosperms have underground stems meant for storage and perennation.
s: The assertion is true: a young (primary) stem is generally green and later often becomes woody and dark brown. The reason is false: most angiosperms do not have underground stems; underground stems for storage and perennation occur only in some plants such as potato, ginger and Colocasia. Hence A is true and R is false.
o: A is true, R is false.
Both A and R are true, R is not correct explantion of A.
Both A and R are true, R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are false

t: Similarity shared by the families Asteraceae and Poaceae is that : there is
s: Both Asteraceae (sunflower) and Poaceae (grasses) have a unilocular ovary with a single ovule attached at its base, i.e. basal placentation. Grass florets are not actinomorphic or pentamerous, and grasses have a superior ovary (hypogynous), while Asteraceae is epigynous. Hence basal placentation is the shared feature.

t: Which among the following description is incorrect about hypogynous flower ?
s: In a hypogynous flower the gynoecium sits at the highest point on a convex or dome-shaped thalamus, its lateral wall is free from the thalamus, and other floral parts lie below it, so the ovary is superior. Examples are China rose, mustard and brinjal. A half-inferior ovary is a feature of perigynous flowers, so C is incorrect.
o: Lateral wall of ovary is free from thalamus
Common examples are China rose, Mustard and Brinjal

t: The distinguishing characteristics of a parthenocarpic fruit is
s: A parthenocarpic fruit develops without fertilisation, so no seeds are formed, and the fruit is seedless, as in banana. The pericarp need not be fleshy or three-layered, the thalamus being edible is a feature of false fruits like apple, and many-seeded fruits arise after fertilisation. Hence seedlessness is the distinguishing feature.
o: Pericarp is fleshy and is always three layered
Thalamus becomes the edible part of fruit

t: The edible part of ginger and turmeric are found below the soil and is identified as a stem due to the
s:
The correct answer is (D) All the above.

Ginger and turmeric are underground modified stems known as rhizomes, which are adapted for food storage and perennation. Morphologically, an organ is identified as a stem rather than a root if it possesses nodes and internodes, scale leaves borne at the nodes, and axillary or terminal buds. 

Since ginger and turmeric display distinct nodes and internodes, possess non-green protective scale leaves, and have buds that can sprout into aerial shoots, all these characteristics confirm their stem nature. 

Options (A), (B), and (C) are each valid distinguishing features of a stem, making (D) the complete and correct response.
o: Presence of scale leaf at the node
Presence of axillary bud on the node

t:
Read the following statements.
Statement A : Generally petals are green, leaf like and protect the flower in the bud stage.
Statement B : There may be a variation in the length of filaments within a flower as in Salvia and Mustard.
s:
Correct Answer: (D) Statement A is incorrect, B is correct.

Explanation:
Statement A is incorrect because sepals, not petals, are generally green, leaf-like, and protect the flower in the bud stage. Petals are usually brightly colored to attract pollinators. 

Statement B is correct because the length of filaments in stamens can vary within the same flower, which is seen in plants like Salvia and Mustard (didynamous and tetradynamous conditions). 

Therefore, options (A), (B), and (C) are wrong because they misidentify the accuracy of either Statement A or Statement B.
o: Statement A and B are correct.
Statement A and B are incorrect.
Statement A is correct, B is incorrect.
Statement A is incorrect, B is correct.

t: Which among the following sentence is wrong about the characteristics of stem
s: The stem bears nodes and internodes, has apical (terminal) and axillary buds, and contains mechanical tissues such as collenchyma and sclerenchyma. Axillary buds develop into lateral branches (or flowers, thorns, tendrils), not into leaves; leaves arise from the nodes. Hence D is the wrong statement.
o: Axis is divisible into nodes and internodes
Presence of two types of buds - Apical and axillary
Presence of mechanical tissues like collenchyma and / or sclerenchyma
Development of axillary buds into leaf

t:
An axillary bud can be present in the
a) axil of petiole of simple leaf
b) axil of petiole or rachis of compound leaf
c) axil of leaflet of compound leaf
s:
Correct Answer: (A) a and b

Concept:
An axillary bud is located in the axil of the petiole of both simple leaves and compound leaves. However, buds are never present in the axil of leaflets of a compound leaf, which is a key morphological feature used to distinguish a leaflet from a simple leaf. 

Why other options are wrong:
Statement (c) is incorrect because leaflets lack axillary buds. Therefore, any option containing (c)—namely (B), (C), and (D)—is incorrect.

t:
Assertion (A) : Citrus and Bougainvillea possess stem thorns as it is found in the axil of leaf
Reason (R) : In Euphorbia the entire stem is modified into green flattened structure meant for photosynthesis
s: The assertion is true: thorns of Citrus and Bougainvillea arise in the axil of leaves, showing they are modified axillary buds or stems. The reason is false: the stem of Euphorbia is fleshy and cylindrical, while the flattened green photosynthetic stem (phylloclade) is seen in Opuntia. Hence A is true and R is false.
o: Both A and R are true, R is correct explanation A
Both A and R are true R is not correct explanation A
A is true, R is false
Both A and R are false

t: In Salvia and Mustard, the androecium contains
s: Salvia has only two stamens, while mustard has six; in both the filaments vary in length within a flower (mustard is tetradynamous with four long and two short stamens, and Salvia has unequal stamens). Thus the androecium of these plants differs in stamen number and shows variation in filament length. Hence option B.
o: Same number of stamens and with same height
Difference in the number of stamens and variation in height of filament of stamen
Difference in the number of stamen but with same height for all stamens
Same number of stamens but with variation height of filament of stamen

t:
How many of the following statements are correct
a) In some plants like Lily, Calyx and Corolla are not distinct and are termed as perianth
b) In China rose and Mustard flowers are unisexual
c) Pedicel is the inflorescence axis on which many flowers are arranged
d) Flower is a modified shoot meant for sexual reproduction
s: a is correct: in lily, calyx and corolla are not distinct and are called perianth. d is correct: a flower is a modified shoot for sexual reproduction. b is wrong because China rose and mustard have bisexual flowers. c is wrong since the axis bearing many flowers is the peduncle; the pedicel is the stalk of a single flower. Hence a and d.
o: Only a and c are correct
Only b and d are correct
Only a and d are correct
Only b and c are correct

t: Which among the following is not correct about a perigynous flower
s:
In a perigynous flower, the gynoecium lies in the center while other floral parts are situated on the rim of a cup-shaped or concave thalamus at almost the same level. The ovary is half inferior because its lateral wall remains completely free from the thalamus. Fusion of the ovary wall with the thalamus is a characteristic feature of epigynous flowers, not perigynous flowers.

Options (A), (B), and (D) are correct statements: the thalamus is cup-shaped, the ovary is half inferior, and classic examples include plum, rose, and peach. 

Therefore, statement (C) is incorrect.

Correct Answer: (C) Lateral wall of ovary is fused with thalamus
o: Thalamus is slightly concave and almost like a cup
Lateral wall of ovary is fused with thalamus
Plants like Rose, Plum, Peach etc. possess perigynous flower

t: Which among the following is not a character of pea family
s: Fabaceae (pea family) has bisexual zygomorphic flowers, papilionaceous corolla with vexillary aestivation, diadelphous stamens, and a monocarpellary superior ovary with marginal placentation. An obliquely placed ovary with swollen placenta is characteristic of Solanaceae, not Fabaceae. Hence C.
o: Obliquely placed ovary with swollen placenta
Bisexual zygomorphic flower with diadelphous androecium

t: A root system which have no correlation with radicle of embryo is
s: Adventitious roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle, such as stem nodes, leaves or the base of the stem (e.g. Monstera, banyan prop roots, grass). The tap root develops directly from the radicle, and the fibrous root system of monocots begins after the radicle-derived primary root. Hence adventitious root system.

t:
How many among the following plant possess tap root modified for storage:
Carrot, Turnip, Sweet potato, Radish, Banyan tree
s: Carrot, turnip and radish have swollen tap roots storing food, so three plants qualify. Sweet potato stores food in adventitious root tubers, not in the tap root. Banyan has prop roots, which are adventitious roots for support rather than storage. Hence the count is 3.

t: The underground stems of Ginger and Zaminkand is modified for
s: Ginger (rhizome) and zaminkand (corm) are underground stem modifications. They store food reserves and remain dormant underground during unfavourable conditions, then produce new aerial shoots, so they serve both storage and perennation. They lack chlorophyll and do not photosynthesise. Hence storage and perennation.

t: Plants like Grass, Strawberry, Pistia, Eichhornia etc. possess modified stems meant for
s: Grass and strawberry have runners and stolons, while Pistia and Eichhornia have offsets, short lateral stems with rosettes of leaves that root at nodes. These modified sub-aerial stems produce new plants when they separate, so they function in vegetative propagation, not photosynthesis, storage or mechanical support.

t: How many leaves are present at a node of Alstonia
s: Alstonia shows whorled phyllotaxy, where more than two leaves (often three to many) arise at each node and form a whorl. Alternate phyllotaxy (one leaf per node) is seen in China rose and mustard, and opposite (two per node) in Calotropis and guava. Hence three to many leaves.

t: The axis of inflorescence to which many flowers are connected is
s: The main axis of an inflorescence on which many flowers are arranged is called the peduncle. The pedicel is the stalk of an individual flower, and the thalamus (receptacle) is the swollen end of the pedicel bearing the floral whorls. Hence peduncle, option B.

t: The term 'rachis' is applicable to the
s:
Correct Answer: (C) Stalk of compound leaf

Explanation:
A rachis is the central elongated axis or stalk of a pinnately compound leaf that bears leaflets along its length, representing the continuation of the petiole. 

Why the other options are wrong:
- (A) The stalk of a simple leaf is termed a petiole.
- (B) The stalk of an individual flower is called a pedicel.
- (D) The main stalk of an inflorescence is referred to as a peduncle.

t: Vexillary aestivation is commonly found in
s: Vexillary aestivation is seen in the papilionaceous corolla of Fabaceae (pea, bean). The largest posterior petal (standard or vexillum) overlaps the two lateral wings, which overlap the two smallest anterior keel petals. The calyx of Fabaceae and the corolla of Solanaceae show valvate aestivation. Hence corolla of Fabaceae.

t: The aleurone layer found in the monocot seed is part of
s: In monocot seeds such as maize, the bulky endosperm is separated from the embryo; its outer protein-rich layer, just below the fused seed coat and fruit wall, is the aleurone layer. It is therefore part of the endosperm, not the embryo, seed coat or pericarp. Hence B.

t:
Observe the following diagram of aestivation and identify it :
[[img:c087aaeefe5e]]
s: Imbricate aestivation is one in which the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction, so typically one member is fully outside, one fully inside and the rest partly overlapped, as in Cassia and Gulmohar. Valvate margins just touch, twisted shows each overlapping the next regularly, and vexillary is the pea pattern. The key marks the diagram as imbricate.

t: Which among the following is not a character of Fabaceae
s: Fabaceae flowers have diadelphous androecium (9 + 1 stamens), marginal placentation in a monocarpellary ovary, and a papilionaceous corolla. Epipetalous stamens (fused to petals) are characteristic of Solanaceae, such as brinjal, not Fabaceae, where stamens are free from the corolla. Hence D.

t:
Read the following statements and select the correct option
Statement-I : In Bougainvillea and Citrus, thorns are the modification of axillary bud/stem
Statement-II : In Opuntia, the aerial stem is modified into green fleshy cylindrical structure to carry out photosynthesis
s: Statement I is correct: thorns of Citrus and Bougainvillea arise in leaf axils, showing they are modified axillary buds or stems. Statement II is wrong: in Opuntia the stem is modified into a flattened green structure (phylloclade); the fleshy cylindrical photosynthetic stem is that of Euphorbia. Hence C.
o: Statement I an II are incorrect
Statement-I is correct, and statement-II is wrong
Statement-I is wrong and statement-II is correct

t: Choose the set of plants in which the ovary is superior
s:
In hypogynous flowers, the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other floral parts are situated below it, which makes the ovary superior. Standard NCERT examples of plants with a superior ovary are Mustard, Brinjal, and China rose.

Evaluation of other options:
- (A) Plum, Rose, and Peach have perigynous flowers where the ovary is half-inferior.
- (C) Guava, Cucumber, and ray florets of Sunflower have epigynous flowers where the ovary is inferior.
- (D) Plum has a half-inferior ovary and Guava has an inferior ovary, so this set is mixed.

Correct Answer: (B) Mustard, Brinjal, China rose
o: Guava, Cucumber, Ray florets of Sunflower

t: Identify the common character shared by the flower of Poaceae and Asteraceae
s: Both Poaceae (grasses) and Asteraceae (sunflower) have a unilocular ovary with a single ovule attached at its base, i.e. basal placentation. Grasses have a superior ovary and are not pentamerous, and neither family has a tricarpellary gynoecium (both are bicarpellary). Hence basal placentation is the shared feature.

t: Which among the following plant modify their stems into flattened green structure meant for photosynthesis
s: In Opuntia the stem is modified into a flattened green structure (phylloclade) that carries out photosynthesis, while leaves are reduced to spines. Euphorbia has a fleshy cylindrical green stem, and ginger and zaminkand have underground storage stems. Hence Opuntia.

t: Which among the following type of root system possess a long lived primary root
s: In dicots, the primary root arising from the radicle grows long and persists, bearing lateral roots of several orders to form a tap root system. In monocots the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by fibrous roots from the stem base, and adventitious roots arise from parts other than the radicle. Hence tap root system.

t: How many leaf /leaves is present in a node of stem with alternate phyllotaxy
s:
Phyllotaxy refers to the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch. In alternate phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in an alternate manner, as seen in China rose, mustard, and sunflower plants. Therefore, exactly one leaf is present at each node. 

Why other options are incorrect:
- (B) Two leaves at each node characterize opposite phyllotaxy (e.g., Calotropis, guava).
- (C) and (D) More than two leaves (five or many) arising at a single node form a whorl, which characterizes whorled phyllotaxy (e.g., Alstonia).

Correct Answer: (A) One

t:
Read the following statements and identify the correct option.
Statement A : Stem is usually/ generally green when young and later often become woody and dark brown.
Statement B : In monocotyledons the primary root is long lived and is replaced by a large number of roots which constitute the fibrous root system.
s: Statement A is correct: the stem is generally green when young and later often becomes woody and dark brown. Statement B is incorrect: in monocots the primary root is short-lived, not long-lived, and is replaced by many roots from the base of the stem forming the fibrous root system. Hence A correct, B incorrect.

Statement A and B are incorrect

t: Which among the following sentence is correct about the meristematic region of root ?
s: The region of meristematic activity just behind the root cap has very small, thin-walled cells with dense protoplasm that divide repeatedly; root tips are also a site of growth regulator (e.g. cytokinin) synthesis. Thick walls do not occur here, and root hairs and water absorption belong to the zone of maturation. Hence C.
o: Cells are thick walled with little amount of protoplasm
Abundance of root hairs in this region
Growth regulators are formed in this region
Water is absorbed through this area

t:
Consider the following statements.
Statement A : The stem may not always be typically what they are expected to be, they are often modified to perform different functions.
Statement B : Stem is the descending axis of shoot developing from plumule of embryo.
s: Statement A is correct: stems are often modified to perform functions such as storage, support, protection and propagation. Statement B is incorrect: the stem is the ascending part of the axis bearing branches, leaves, flowers and fruits, developing from the plumule; the root is the descending axis from the radicle. Hence A correct, B incorrect.
o: Statement A and B are correct
Statement A and B are incorrect
Statement A is correct, B is incorrect
Statement A is incorrect, B is correct

t: prop root and stilt root having the similarity in that, both are
s: Prop roots (banyan) arise from branches and stilt roots (maize, sugarcane) arise from lower stem nodes. Both develop from parts other than the radicle, so they are adventitious in origin, and both give mechanical support. They are not tap root modifications, they are aerial roots entering the soil, and they are not typical of halophytes.

t:
Assertion (A) : In calotropis and Guava, one node possess two leaf.
Reason (R) : Opposite phyllotaxy is present in Calotropis and Guava.
s: In opposite phyllotaxy, a pair of leaves arises at each node and lies opposite each other, as in Calotropis and guava. That is exactly why one node in these plants bears two leaves. So both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
o: Both A and R are true, R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, R is not correct explanation of A
A is true, R is false
Both A and R are false

t: Which among the following sentence is wrong ?
s: Thorns, as in Citrus and Bougainvillea, are hard, woody, straight and pointed modified axillary buds with exogenous origin, protecting plants from grazing animals. Describing them as non-woody, curved and endogenous is wrong. A, C and D are correct statements about stems, stem tendrils, and photosynthetic stems of Opuntia and Euphorbia. Hence B.
o: Stem is generally green when young and later often become woody and dark brown

t: The term venation is applicable to

Option (A) is incorrect because roots generally do not bear buds; apical and axillary buds are characteristic of stems.
Option (B) is incorrect because roots lack nodes and internodes, which are exclusive features of the shoot axis.

t: Which among the following sentence is not correct about cymose inflorescence
s:
In a cymose inflorescence, the main axis (peduncle) terminates in a flower, which limits its continuation. Therefore, the peduncle exhibits definite (determinate) growth, not indefinite growth. 

Flowers in cymose inflorescence develop in a basipetal order, meaning the oldest flower is at the apex and the youngest flower is at the base. 

- Option (A) is correct for cymose inflorescence as maturation is basipetal.
- Option (C) is correct because the peduncle terminates in a flower.
- Option (D) is correct because younger flowers arise lower down the axis.

Therefore, the incorrect statement is (B) Indefinite growth of peduncle.
